t.2.45.1: Guha, scorched by grief, spoke these words to Lakṣmaṇa, the Rāghava, who was keeping watch sincerely for his brother's sake.
t.2.45.2: Dear one, this comfortable bed has been prepared for your sake; rest well upon it, O prince, and refresh yourself as you please.
t.2.45.3: All these people here are accustomed to hardships, but you are accustomed to comfort. We shall stay awake through the night to guard Kākutstha.
t.2.45.4: For there is no one on earth dearer to me than Rāma; I speak this truth, and by truth itself I swear it to you.
t.2.45.5: Through his grace I hope to win very great fame in this world, an abundant attainment of dharma, and a complete attainment of wealth.
t.2.45.6: Therefore I, bow in hand, together with my kinsmen, will guard on every side my dear friend Rāma as he lies sleeping with Sītā.
t.2.45.7: For nothing in this forest is unknown to me, since I roam it always; indeed, we could withstand even a very great army of four divisions.
t.2.45.9: When the son of Daśaratha lies upon the bare ground together with Sītā, how can I obtain sleep, or life, or any comforts?
t.2.45.8: Then Lakṣmaṇa said to him: "O sinless one, protected as we are by you, who look to dharma alone, none of us is afraid here."
t.2.45.10: He who could not be overcome in battle by all the gods and asuras together, behold him now lying at ease upon the grass together with Sītā.
t.2.45.11: He who was obtained through the austerity of mantras and through manifold toils, this is the one son of Daśaratha, bearing marks worthy of him.
t.2.45.13: Having raised a very great cry, the women have fallen silent from exhaustion; I think, dear son, the king's palace has now ceased its clamor.
t.2.45.12: With this one gone into exile, the king will not live long; surely the earth will very soon become a widow.
t.2.45.15: My own mother might indeed survive, through the watchful care of Śatrughna; but the grief is this, that Kausalyā, mother of a hero, will perish.
t.2.45.14: Kausalyā and the king, and likewise my own mother: I have no hope that all of them will live through this night.
t.2.45.16: That city, thronged with devoted people, pleasant to behold and bringing delight, now caught up in the king's misfortune, will perish.
t.2.45.17: Without attaining his heart's desire, now lost, lost beyond recall, and without installing Rāma in the kingship, my father will perish.
t.2.45.18: When that time has indeed arrived, they, their purpose accomplished, will perform all the funeral rites for their father, the king, who has passed away.
t.2.45.20: That city, thronged with chariots, horses and elephants, resounding with the sound of musical instruments, filled with every kind of auspicious thing, and crowded with joyful and well-nourished people.
t.2.45.19: The city with its charming squares and well-laid-out highways, rich in mansions and palaces, and graced by the finest courtesans.
t.2.45.21: Happy, they will roam through my father's royal city, rich in pleasure groves and gardens and resplendent with assemblies and festivals.
t.2.45.22: May we, when this dwelling in the forest has come to an end, enter Ayodhyā together with him who is true to his promise, safe and well!
t.2.45.23: That night passed for the great-souled prince as he stood there, lamenting and stricken with sorrow.
t.2.45.24: As the king's son, devoted to the welfare of the people, spoke the truth thus, Guha, out of deep affection for his elder, shed tears, crushed by calamity, like an elephant tormented by fever and racked with pain.
